verbs.summary: Draw the user's attention to one element without activating it. Use this before acting on something so the person watching knows where to look; a guided demo or a walkthrough is mostly this verb. Does not click, submit or change anything.

selector.description: CSS selector for the element. Prefer a stable id over a positional selector, so the call survives a redesign.

elementId.description: Element id, as an alternative to a selector.

label.description: Short text to show beside it, explaining why it matters.

scroll.description: Bring it into view first if it is off screen. Defaults to true.

found.description: False when nothing matched, so a caller can skip rather than point at nothing.

rect.description: Where it is now, in viewport pixels. Measured at call time, because that is what lets the same instruction work against a layout that has since changed.

verbs.summary: Stop drawing attention to anything. Call this when a walkthrough ends or is cancelled, so the interface is left as it was found.
